title: The Color Mystery of Mantis Shrimp
hook: Mantis shrimp have up to 16 color receptors — so what do they see?
script: Mantis shrimp have up to 16 color receptors — so what do they see? This means they can theoretically see up to 100,000 different colors, while we can see about 1 million. However, astonishingly, mantis shrimp struggle to differentiate between similar colors, particularly shades of green. This challenges the idea that more receptors equate to better color discrimination. In fact, their eyes work differently, scanning colors like a barcode reader rather than blending them as ours do. Each eye also independently provides a 3D view of their environment, enhancing their perception. Furthermore, they can detect circular polarized light, a capability unique to them among animals.
